title: Algebraization from torsion in the completed conormal differential
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Put $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]^\wedge$ for some integer $r\geq0$, where completion is $I$-adic [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal and let $E=P/J$ be $I$-adically complete. Suppose that, for some $c\geq0$, $I^c$ annihilates the kernel and cokernel of $\delta:J/J^2\to E^{\oplus r}$, $f\bmod J^2\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_{i=1}^r$, using the continuous polynomial derivatives on $P$. Then there is a finite type commutative $A$-algebra $D$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] such that $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism], together with an $A$-algebra isomorphism $D^\wedge\cong E$ of $I$-adic completions.

source.place: Tag 0AKG (lemma-approximate-by-etale-over-complement), with the cohomological condition (3) of Tag 0AJU (lemma-equivalent-with-artin).

proof.text: We prove the assertion simultaneously for every Noetherian base ring and every presentation in the statement, by induction on a finite list of generators $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)$. Such a list exists by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. If $t=0$, then $I=0$ and completion of $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is that polynomial ring itself: all positive-power quotients are the ring. Thus $E=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/J$ is finite type; take $D=E$. The complement of $V(0)$ is empty, so the etale assertion is vacuous. The same argument includes $r=0$ and the zero algebra.

We will use the following elementary observation whenever a finite type model $C$ with $\widehat C_I\cong E$ has been constructed. Apply [lem-per-jacobian-torsion-etale-shrink] to this isomorphism and the original presentation of $E$ to obtain $g=1+x$, $x\in IC$, with $C_g$ etale away from $V(I)$. Set $D=C_g=C[y]/(gy-1)$, a finite type $A$-algebra. For every $n\geq1$, $x^n=0$ modulo $I^nC$, so $g$ has inverse $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(-x)^j$ there. Consequently $C/I^nC\to D/I^nD$ is an isomorphism, with inverse induced by that displayed polynomial in $x$; these maps commute with all quotient transitions. Taking compatible sequences gives $\widehat C_I\cong\widehat D_I$ as $A$-algebras. Thus this observation supplies exactly the required $D$ from any finite type model, without altering its completion.

source.place: Tag 0AKG (lemma-approximate-by-etale-over-complement), omitted small detail; Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), part (2).

proof.text: If $t=1$, apply [lem-per-principal-jacobian-algebraization] with $a=a_1$ to the given presentation and annihilator. It gives a finite type $A$-algebra $C$ with $\widehat C_I\cong E$. Step 2 then gives $D$. This completes the one-generator case. No regularity or non-zero-divisor assumption is made on $a_1$.

Assume $t>1$ and that the full assertion, including the etale complement, holds for ideals with a generating list of length at most $t-1$ over any Noetherian base. Put $a=a_t$ and $K=(a_1,\ldots,a_{t-1})$. For each $m\geq1$ put $A_m=A/(a^m)$ and $K_m=KA_m$. The ring $A_m$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since it is the quotient of $A$ and hence a finite type $A$-algebra. In $A_m$ the image of $a$ is nilpotent, so every prime contains it; therefore $V(IA_m)=V(K_m)$. Apply [lem-per-jacobian-torsion-closed-base-change] with $H=(a^m)$ and ideal $K_m$. We obtain that $E_m=E/a^mE$ is $K_m$-adically complete with a finite completed-polynomial presentation whose conormal kernel and cokernel are killed by a power of $K_m$. The exponent is allowed to depend on $m$; no flatness of $A\to A_m$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0AKA (lemma-approximate), reduction modulo powers of a_t; Tag 0GB2 (lemma-base-change-rig-etale-homomorphism).

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to the presentations of Step 4 over $A_m$ and the generating list of $K_m$ of length $t-1$. For every $m\geq1$ it gives a finite type $A_m$-algebra $C_m$, etale outside $V(K_m)$, and an $A_m$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{C_m}_{K_m}\cong E/a^mE$. These choices need not be compatible. They are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-per-rig-etale-principal-reduction] for $I=K+(a)$ and the original $E$. That lemma produces an $(a)$-adically complete $A$-algebra $F$, with a finite completed-polynomial presentation having kernel and cokernel killed by a power of $a$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat F_I\cong E$. Its statement includes the assembly of independently chosen quotient models; no compatibility is inferred merely from equality of their completions.

source.place: Tag 0AKA (lemma-approximate), compatible-model construction and principal-complete intermediate algebra B-prime, before the last application of 0ALS.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-principal-jacobian-algebraization] to the presentation of $F$ from Step 5. We get a finite type $A$-algebra $C$ and $\widehat C_{(a)}\cong F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $C$ is Noetherian. Fix $n\geq1$. Complete the exact sequence $0\to I^nC\to C\to C/I^nC\to0$ for the ideal $(a)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]. Its modules are finite since $C$ is Noetherian. The image of the completed first term is $I^n\widehat C_{(a)}$: choose finitely many generators of $I^nC$ and apply the same exactness statement to the surjection from the corresponding finite free $C$-module onto $I^nC$ (its kernel is finite). Since $a^n\in I^n$, the $(a)$-adic completion of $C/I^nC$ is itself, its quotient tower being constant from index $n$ on. Hence the canonical map $C/I^nC\to\widehat C_{(a)}/I^n\widehat C_{(a)}$ is an isomorphism. These are the maps induced by $C\to\widehat C_{(a)}$, so they commute with reduction in $n$. Taking compatible sequences and using $F\cong\widehat C_{(a)}$ gives $\widehat C_I\cong\widehat F_I\cong E$.

source.place: Tag 0AKA (lemma-approximate), final application of 0ALS; nested completion compatibility expanded using exact completion of finite modules (Algebra Tag 00MB, lemma-completion-flat).

proof.text: Apply the observation of Step 2 to the finite type model $C$ of Step 6 and the original isomorphism $\widehat C_I\cong E$. It provides the finite type $A$-algebra $D=C_g$, etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$, and $\widehat D_I\cong E$. This closes the induction, and therefore proves every clause of the statement.
